======================================================================
FINAL EXECUTION — REMOVE RORK AND COMPLETE IVX INDEPENDENCE NOW
MIGRATE, VERIFY, CUT OVER, THEN REVOKE
======================================================================

OWNER DIRECTIVE

Begin the final removal of every operational dependency on Rork.

This is the existing IVX Holdings production platform.
Do not create another application.
Do not restart the project.
Do not delete functioning production code.
Do not disconnect Rork until an IVX-owned replacement is operational,
tested and recoverable.

The current report confirms:

- IVX owns the GitHub repository.
- IVX owns the Render production service.
- IVX owns the Supabase project.
- Production is currently live.
- IVX IA still depends on Rork infrastructure.
- 75 backend tests are failing.
- 9 Expo tests are failing.
- The current quality gate is broken.

The final objective is:

IVX Holdings must own and independently operate its code-generation
engine, autonomous worker, AI provider connections, deployments,
tests, production evidence and recovery process.

======================================================================
RULE ZERO — NO UNSAFE IMMEDIATE DELETION
======================================================================

Do not:

- Delete the Rork project immediately.
- Delete working source files.
- Remove an active dependency before its replacement passes.
- Rotate credentials before verifying owner recovery access.
- Disable production services.
- Change production DNS during development.
- Claim independence from a written plan.
- claim VERIFIED while tests are failing.

Use this mandatory sequence:

INVENTORY
→ BACKUP
→ BUILD REPLACEMENT
→ FIX TESTS
→ VERIFY REPLACEMENT
→ PARALLEL RUN
→ CUTOVER
→ STABILITY TEST
→ ROTATE SECRETS
→ REVOKE RORK
→ FINAL CERTIFICATION

======================================================================
PHASE 1 — FREEZE AND PRESERVE THE CURRENT SYSTEM
======================================================================

1. Identify the canonical IVX GitHub repository and production branch.
2. Record the current GitHub HEAD SHA.
3. Record the current Render production SHA.
4. Confirm GitHub HEAD and production parity.
5. Export the complete environment-variable names without exposing values.
6. Export Supabase schema, migrations and current backup.
7. Export Render service configuration.
8. Export Expo/EAS project configuration and signing ownership.
9. Export AWS IAM, DNS, S3 and CloudFront configuration.
10. Tag the current stable production release:

    pre-rork-removal-stable

11. Create a protected migration branch:

    ivx-rork-independence

12. Create a rollback runbook before changing anything.

Required evidence:

- Repository.
- Branch.
- Commit SHA.
- Render deploy ID.
- Database backup ID.
- Configuration backup location.
- Rollback command.
- Owner confirmation.

======================================================================
PHASE 2 — COMPLETE RORK DEPENDENCY AUDIT
======================================================================

Search the complete source code, infrastructure and runtime for:

- rork.com
- Rork SDK packages.
- Rork APIs.
- Rork webhooks.
- Rork authentication.
- Rork AI gateways.
- Vercel AI Gateway configured or paid through Rork.
- Rork worker services.
- Rork deployment actions.
- Rork telemetry.
- Rork-owned tokens.
- Rork-owned service accounts.
- Rork-specific variables.
- Hidden remote configuration.
- Hardcoded vendor URLs.
- Proprietary code execution endpoints.
- Proprietary prompt or model routing.
- Vendor-managed queues.
- Vendor-managed storage.
- Vendor-controlled billing.
- Vendor-controlled recovery access.

For every dependency return:

- Dependency ID.
- Exact file and line.
- Environment variable.
- Runtime purpose.
- Production impact.
- Replacement component.
- Migration risk.
- Migration status.
- Test required.

Create:

docs/rork-dependency-register.md

Do not mark the audit complete until runtime network logs are also
inspected for connections that may not appear directly in source code.

======================================================================
PHASE 3 — CORRECT ALL CURRENT TEST REGRESSIONS
======================================================================

Current failures reported:

- 75 backend failures.
- 9 Expo failures.
- 6 Expo errors.
- Owner password handlers.
- Passwordless emergency flows.
- Growth reporting.
- Autonomous Ops Dashboard.
- Investor protection.
- Failure recovery service.
- Additional failures shown by the canonical test runner.

Execute the actual repository test commands and create a baseline report.

For every failure:

1. Record test ID.
2. Record affected file.
3. Reproduce failure.
4. Determine root cause.
5. Fix production code or correct an invalid test.
6. Add or strengthen regression coverage.
7. Rerun the individual test.
8. Rerun the affected suite.
9. Rerun the complete canonical suite.

Required final quality gate:

- Backend: 0 failed.
- Expo: 0 failed.
- Expo execution errors: 0.
- TypeScript: 0 errors.
- Critical lint errors: 0.
- Build: PASS.
- Security scan: no unresolved critical issue.

Do not hide, skip, quarantine or delete failing tests merely to obtain
a green report.

======================================================================
PHASE 4 — CREATE THE IVX-OWNED AI PROVIDER LAYER
======================================================================

Remove the requirement for Rork’s AI gateway.

Build:

backend/services/ivx-ai-provider/
backend/services/ivx-ai-provider/types.ts
backend/services/ivx-ai-provider/router.ts
backend/services/ivx-ai-provider/providers/
backend/services/ivx-ai-provider/health.ts
backend/services/ivx-ai-provider/cost-control.ts
backend/services/ivx-ai-provider/failover.ts

The IVX provider layer must support owner-configured providers through
standard adapters.

Each adapter must implement:

- Provider health.
- Model selection.
- Chat completion.
- Structured JSON output.
- Tool calling.
- Streaming where required.
- Timeout.
- AbortController cancellation.
- Retry.
- Backoff.
- Error normalization.
- Token usage.
- Cost tracking.
- Provider failover.
- Rate-limit handling.
- Logging without secrets.

Owner controls:

- Enable provider.
- Disable provider.
- Select primary provider.
- Select fallback provider.
- Select model by task type.
- Set daily spending limit.
- Set monthly spending limit.
- Emergency stop.

Requirements:

- Provider credentials belong to IVX.
- Provider credentials remain server-side.
- No key is embedded in mobile or web bundles.
- No code-generation request requires a Rork account.
- Rork may not remain as an invisible fallback.

======================================================================
PHASE 5 — BUILD THE IVX-OWNED AUTONOMOUS ENGINE
======================================================================

Replace the Rork-managed autonomous pipeline with an IVX-owned system.

Required components:

1. IVX Task API.
2. IVX task database.
3. IVX durable worker.
4. IVX job queue.
5. IVX code-generation engine.
6. IVX code execution sandbox.
7. IVX repository adapter.
8. IVX test runner.
9. IVX evidence store.
10. IVX approval ledger.
11. IVX deployment adapter.
12. IVX production-verification service.
13. IVX rollback controller.
14. IVX monitoring and alerts.

Mandatory job states:

- QUEUED
- ANALYZING
- PLANNING
- WAITING_FOR_CONTEXT
- CODING
- TESTING
- BLOCKED
- APPROVAL_REQUIRED
- COMMITTING
- DEPLOYING
- VERIFYING
- COMPLETED
- FAILED
- ROLLED_BACK
- CANCELLED

Every job record must persist:

- Job ID.
- Owner request.
- Requirements.
- Technical plan.
- Risk level.
- Repository.
- Branch.
- Base commit.
- Files read.
- Files changed.
- Patch/diff.
- Commands executed.
- Test results.
- Error details.
- Model/provider used.
- Cost.
- Commit SHA.
- Pull request.
- Approval record.
- Deployment ID.
- Production evidence.
- Final result.
- Start/end timestamps.

Completed jobs must never contain a null result.

======================================================================
PHASE 6 — BUILD REAL GENERAL-PURPOSE DEVELOPMENT
======================================================================

The new IVX system must not be limited to one-line proof files or small
patches.

It must be capable of:

- Reading the full IVX architecture.
- Understanding existing patterns.
- Creating several coordinated files.
- Creating complete backend endpoints.
- Creating Expo screens.
- Creating web screens.
- Adding navigation.
- Adding state management.
- Creating database migrations.
- Creating Supabase RLS policies.
- Creating realtime subscriptions.
- Creating notifications.
- Creating unit tests.
- Creating integration tests.
- Creating end-to-end tests.
- Updating documentation.
- Producing rollback plans.

Add planning controls to prevent unlimited context:

- Repository index.
- Relevant-file retrieval.
- Dependency graph.
- Per-stage context limits.
- File-level context budgets.
- Planner model separate from patch model when configured.
- Cancellation of hung provider requests.
- Maximum job duration.
- Heartbeats.
- Safe retries.
- Partial progress persistence.

======================================================================
PHASE 7 — PROVE SENIOR-DEVELOPER CAPABILITY
======================================================================

Complete all tests below using the IVX-owned system, not the Rork UI.

TEST 1 — REAL BUG FIX

- Select one existing reproducible defect.
- Reproduce it.
- Identify root cause.
- Fix it.
- Add a regression test.
- Commit it.
- Verify the fix.

TEST 2 — MULTI-FILE BACKEND FEATURE

Build an owner-approved backend feature containing:

- API route.
- Service layer.
- Validation.
- Authentication.
- Authorization.
- Database persistence.
- Logs.
- Tests.
- Documentation.

TEST 3 — FULL-STACK FEATURE

Build one meaningful IVX feature containing:

- Database migration.
- RLS.
- Backend API.
- Mobile or web interface.
- State management.
- Error handling.
- Tests.
- Production-safe documentation.

A constant, health endpoint or ten-line demonstration does not qualify.

TEST 4 — REFACTOR

- Select a duplicated or fragile subsystem.
- Refactor it.
- Preserve behavior.
- Add tests.
- Prove no regression.

TEST 5 — INCIDENT RECOVERY

- Simulate a controlled failure.
- Detect it.
- Diagnose it.
- Recover.
- Verify health.
- Produce a root-cause report.

TEST 6 — DEPLOYMENT

- Create branch.
- Create commit.
- Run the complete quality gate.
- Request signed owner approval.
- Deploy.
- Verify `/health` and `/version`.
- Confirm production SHA.

TEST 7 — ROLLBACK

- Execute a controlled rollback drill.
- Verify previous stable SHA.
- Verify database integrity.
- Record recovery time.

TEST 8 — RORK-BLOCKED TEST

In a controlled environment:

- Block Rork domains.
- Remove Rork credentials.
- Start the IVX-owned worker.
- Submit a real multi-file development task.
- Generate code.
- Run tests.
- Create a commit.
- Create evidence.
- Prepare deployment.

This test must pass before Rork is revoked.

======================================================================
PHASE 8 — INDEPENDENT IVX IA CHAT
======================================================================

Move IVX IA chat into IVX-owned production infrastructure.

Requirements:

- IVX-owned URL.
- IVX authentication.
- Owner role verification.
- Persistent conversations.
- Stable conversation IDs.
- Stable message IDs.
- Correct chronological order.
- No duplicates.
- Search.
- Attachments.
- Job creation.
- Job status.
- Test evidence.
- Deployment evidence.
- Approval requests.
- Production reports.
- Provider selection.
- Emergency stop.

IVX IA chat must continue operating while rork.com is blocked.

======================================================================
PHASE 9 — OWNER-CONTROLLED GITHUB AND DEPLOYMENT
======================================================================

GitHub requirements:

- Repository owned by IVX.
- Owner is organization administrator.
- Protected main branch.
- Required pull requests.
- Required checks.
- Required test suite.
- Secret scanning.
- Dependency scanning.
- No Rork-exclusive deploy key.
- No unidentified webhook.
- No vendor-owned GitHub App with unrestricted access.

Deployment requirements:

- IVX-controlled Render account.
- IVX-controlled deploy hook.
- IVX-controlled billing.
- IVX-controlled variables.
- Exact commit deployment.
- Signed single-use approval.
- Rollback capability.
- Health verification.
- Production SHA parity.

Deployments must not originate from Rork infrastructure after cutover.

======================================================================
PHASE 10 — COMPLETE OWNERSHIP AND CREDENTIAL AUDIT
======================================================================

Audit these systems:

- GitHub.
- Render.
- Supabase.
- AWS.
- Expo/EAS.
- Domain registrar.
- DNS.
- Email.
- AI providers.
- Monitoring.
- Error tracking.
- Messaging.
- Payments.
- Storage.
- Backups.

For every system verify:

- Legal/account owner.
- Billing owner.
- Primary administrator.
- Recovery email.
- Recovery phone.
- MFA.
- Active users.
- Service accounts.
- API keys.
- Webhooks.
- Deployment access.
- Last credential rotation.

Before removing Rork:

1. Confirm IVX owner access.
2. Confirm backup access.
3. Confirm recovery access.
4. Test a fresh login.
5. Test MFA.
6. Test deployment.
7. Test rollback.
8. Test provider billing.
9. Test production recovery.

Never expose credentials in the report.

======================================================================
PHASE 11 — PARALLEL OPERATION
======================================================================

Run the IVX-owned system in parallel before cutover.

Minimum parallel validation:

- 20 successful development jobs.
- At least 5 meaningful multi-file jobs.
- 100 consecutive provider calls with measured reliability.
- Zero lost job results.
- Zero duplicate commits.
- Zero unauthorized deployments.
- Successful restart recovery.
- Successful Render restart recovery.
- Successful queue recovery.
- Successful provider failover.
- Successful Rork-blocked execution.
- Full test suite passing.

Compare:

- Job completion.
- Accuracy.
- Runtime.
- Cost.
- Failure rate.
- Retry rate.
- Test quality.
- Evidence quality.

======================================================================
PHASE 12 — CUTOVER FROM RORK
======================================================================

Only perform cutover after Phases 1–11 are VERIFIED.

Cutover sequence:

1. Create final database and repository backups.
2. Freeze production deployments.
3. Record final Rork-dependent production state.
4. Enable the IVX provider layer.
5. Enable the IVX autonomous worker.
6. Enable the IVX job queue.
7. Enable the IVX chat interface.
8. Redirect internal development tasks to IVX.
9. Disable Rork as an AI fallback.
10. Disable Rork deployment actions.
11. Disable Rork autonomous-worker access.
12. Remove Rork webhooks.
13. Remove Rork GitHub access.
14. Remove Rork Render access.
15. Remove Rork Supabase access.
16. Remove Rork AWS access.
17. Rotate all credentials previously accessible by Rork.
18. Rebuild/redeploy with the rotated credentials.
19. Verify all production modules.
20. Unfreeze owner-approved deployments.

Do not delete historical Rork accounts until evidence and billing records
have been preserved.

======================================================================
PHASE 13 — POST-CUTOVER QA
======================================================================

Verify in production:

- Owner login.
- Owner MFA.
- Session persistence.
- Member registration.
- Investor registration.
- Buyer registration.
- Database synchronization.
- IVX IA chat.
- Autonomous job creation.
- Code generation.
- Multi-file changes.
- Test execution.
- Commit creation.
- Owner approval.
- Deployment.
- Production verification.
- Rollback.
- Members.
- Investors.
- Buyers.
- Properties.
- Deals.
- Reels.
- Media.
- Documents.
- Notifications.
- Search.
- Filters.
- Payments configuration.
- Global intelligence endpoints.
- Dashboard.
- Monitoring.
- Backups.

Verify Android, web and iOS-compatible behavior where applicable.

Required outcome:

- 0 critical failures.
- 0 failed canonical tests.
- 0 Rork network requests.
- 0 Rork credentials.
- 0 Rork deployment authority.
- 0 hidden Rork runtime dependencies.

======================================================================
PHASE 14 — 72-HOUR INDEPENDENCE VALIDATION
======================================================================

Operate without Rork for 72 hours.

Continuously verify:

- API health.
- Database health.
- AI provider health.
- Worker health.
- Queue health.
- Chat health.
- Error rates.
- Latency.
- Job persistence.
- Build reliability.
- Deployment traceability.
- Cost.
- Security alerts.

Complete at least:

- 10 additional autonomous jobs.
- 2 multi-file feature tasks.
- 2 bug fixes.
- 1 controlled deployment.
- 1 rollback drill.
- 1 provider failover drill.
- 1 service restart drill.

======================================================================
FINAL REQUIRED EVIDENCE
======================================================================

Return one evidence package containing:

1. Canonical GitHub repository.
2. Canonical production branch.
3. Final commit SHA.
4. Production commit SHA.
5. GitHub/production parity.
6. CI run ID.
7. Complete test totals.
8. 0-failure proof.
9. Render service ID.
10. Render deployment ID.
11. `/health` HTTP 200.
12. `/version` response.
13. Supabase migration version.
14. AI provider ownership proof without secret values.
15. IVX worker job IDs.
16. Meaningful multi-file task proof.
17. Owner approval proof.
18. Rollback proof.
19. Rork-blocked test proof.
20. Runtime network audit proving zero Rork requests.
21. Credential rotation checklist.
22. Access-revocation checklist.
23. 72-hour stability report.
24. Remaining risks.
25. Owner acceptance.

======================================================================
FINAL STATUS RULES
======================================================================

Use only:

- NOT STARTED
- IN PROGRESS
- BLOCKED
- FAILED
- VERIFIED

Do not mark VERIFIED based on:

- A narrative.
- A screenshot.
- A plan.
- A single endpoint.
- A one-line generated file.
- A commit without tests.
- Historical evidence.
- Mock data.
- A test executed on the wrong commit.
- A production check without SHA parity.

======================================================================
FINAL CERTIFICATION
======================================================================

Return:

IVX FULL INDEPENDENCE FROM RORK:
VERIFIED / BLOCKED / FAILED

Rork may be considered removed only when:

- The full canonical test suite passes.
- IVX owns its AI-provider accounts.
- IVX owns the autonomous worker.
- IVX owns the job queue and task database.
- IVX IA chat runs independently.
- A meaningful full-stack task is completed without Rork.
- Deployment is controlled by IVX.
- Rollback is verified.
- All credentials previously accessible by Rork are rotated.
- Rork access is revoked.
- Runtime produces zero requests to Rork.
- The 72-hour independence test passes.

FINAL REQUIRED RESULT:

IVX owns its source code.
IVX owns its infrastructure.
IVX owns its AI provider layer.
IVX owns its autonomous development engine.
IVX owns its data.
IVX owns its deployments.
IVX owns its credentials.
IVX controls all approvals.
Rork is not required to build, operate, deploy or recover IVX Holdings.
======================================================================
